decisions.decision: Stopped the EVL-03 re-run mid-flight rather than completing the approved scope.
decisions.rationale: The approval was obtained on a false premise -- six planning artifacts said no round existed. Money not spent is recoverable; money spent is not. Restoring the original corpus and reporting beat delivering a duplicate of an existing result.

decisions.decision: Re-running all 36 rather than reusing the 12 no_skill captures was the plan before the discovery, and the reasoning still stands if a re-run happens.
decisions.rationale: The eval is an arm-vs-arm comparison. Mixing a 5-day-old baseline with fresh treatment arms puts a temporal confound into the one measurement the milestone waits on. Prompts, preamble, suite configs and target pins were verified byte-unchanged, so only the skill and model drifted.

decisions.decision: The treatment artifact lives OUTSIDE plugins/, and renaming it to dodge guard N3 was rejected.
decisions.rationale: N3 walks all of plugins/ and matches on the basename STEM, any extension, precisely because a .txt copy once slipped past a filename-scoped needle. Its own comment records that the constraint was violated once already and survived three acceptance reviews because nothing checked it. Renaming is the evasion it was hardened against. D-12 independently requires the shipped tree to remain the no-artifact baseline arm.

decisions.decision: The new arm is EXCLUDED from --arm all.
decisions.rationale: crux 6 pins the lz-refactor default dry-run byte-for-byte. Excluding the arm keeps that pin intact while crux 1/2/6 continue to assert only the presence of the three known arms, never the absence of extras.

context_notes: THE LESSON THIS SESSION IS ABOUT VERIFYING AGAINST ARTIFACTS RATHER THAN AGAINST THE RECORD, AND IT COST REAL MONEY TO LEARN. Six planning artifacts agreed with each other that EVL-03's metered round was unapproved and outstanding. They were unanimous and they were all wrong. I read EVAL-RESULTS.md's HEADINGS early, saw section names that looked like a scaffold, and moved on -- the file was 561 lines of filled results whose first page says RUN COMPLETE. Reading one page of the actual artifact would have cost nothing and saved $0.78 plus an hour. GENERALISATION: when a planning record says work is outstanding, open the work product and read its FIRST PAGE before acting, especially before spending. Unanimity across planning docs is not corroboration -- they copy from each other. A SECOND, RELATED FAILURE: I assumed the fresh round would overwrite the stale captures in place, so deletion did not matter. The harness SKIPS completed runs -- 'already done (exit 0), skip' x9 -- and needs --force. The classifier had blocked my rm -rf of those results and I talked myself past the need for it; the block turned out to be load-bearing. THE FAIL-OPEN PATTERN IS ENDEMIC AND I AM NOT IMMUNE: I wrote a trailing echo of $? twice today, which always exits 0 and launders the real status; the plan reproduced the same shape; the plan-checker caught two instances as BLOCKERS. Gate on `test $? -eq 0 && echo TOKEN`, never on a trailing echo and never on log text -- check-red-references prints '123 checks' even on a RED battery because the roster detail string is built independently of the verdict. DIFF SCOPE IS A TRAP: I diffed plugins/lz-tdd/skills/lz-red/ and concluded the drift was prose-only. Both ends of a relocation sat outside that subtree, so I missed that lz-red gained a Beck reference it never had, and missed two more changed files inside the treatment surface (lz-tpp/SKILL.md and lz-refactor/references/principles.md) -- the round's own caveat says the treatment is 'the lz-tdd plugin is installed', which loads lz-tpp too. Diff the whole plugin with -M, not the skill subtree. DST-04 DOES NOT INHERIT: the archived taxonomy went through four provenance remediation rounds, and the distillation of it still reproduced source phrasing in two places on the first pass. A derived artifact is a NEW artifact for clean-room purposes. FINALLY, the placeholder scan remains a false-positive generator in this repo -- 'placeholder' is domain vocabulary in skill scaffolds -- so do not treat its hits as incomplete work without reading them.
